passage:
Sunday.
Registered for another course today. That's the fourth: data structures, then cloud basics, then a portfolio workshop, now advanced SQL. Simran got a callback last week, and I was happy for her, and jealous, and also relieved that it wasn't me. I keep telling myself: once I finish this one, I'll be ready to apply. I said the same in March. The truth I don't want to write down: what scares me is the email that says we regret to inform you. As long as I'm learning, I can't be rejected. It's a comfortable place, and it is costing me months. I looked at the job list, and closed it, and paid for the course anyway.
— Keerthana

qa.q: How many courses has Keerthana registered for so far?
qa.a: Keerthana says this is the fourth course.

qa.q: What does Keerthana feel is really behind the delay?
qa.a: Keerthana admits fear of rejection, the email that says we regret to inform you, is driving the delay.

qa.q: What could Keerthana do instead of another course?
qa.a: Keerthana could apply to one role a week while learning, since real applications give feedback that a course cannot.

qa.q: How might Simran see Keerthana's delay?
qa.a: Simran may not see the fear and may think Keerthana is being thorough, so a friend could gently encourage Keerthana to apply.

grounding: A student keeps taking one more course before applying, saying the time is not right, while fear of rejection quietly drives the delay for months.

passage:
Joseph: applied anywhere yet?
Dilnaz: not yet. finishing the cloud course first
Joseph: that's what you said about the data course in June
Dilnaz: that one was basic. employers want cloud now
Joseph: and before that the SQL one
Dilnaz: ok fine. I just want to be ready
Joseph: Dilnaz you've done 5 courses since March. how many applications
Dilnaz: ...zero
Joseph: what's actually stopping you
Dilnaz: honestly? if I apply and they say no, then it's real. then it means I'm not good enough
Dilnaz: if I'm still "preparing" nobody can reject me
Joseph: that's a pretty expensive way to feel safe
Dilnaz: I know 😔
Joseph: send 3 this week. I'll send 3 too. we tell each other the rejections, not just the wins
Dilnaz: ok. 3. before I start another course

qa.q: How many courses has Dilnaz done since March?
qa.a: Dilnaz has done 5 courses since March.

qa.q: What feeling is really behind Dilnaz's delay?
qa.a: Dilnaz is afraid of rejection, feeling a no would prove not being good enough, so preparing forever feels safer.

qa.q: What else could help Dilnaz take the first step?
qa.a: Dilnaz could apply to a few roles that match current skills and treat each reply, even a no, as a pointer to what to learn next.

qa.q: How does Joseph see the courses?
qa.a: Joseph sees them as a way of hiding from rejection and gently pushes Dilnaz to apply, offering to share rejections too.

grounding: Shows a student taking course after course before applying, saying they are not ready, while fear of rejection quietly drives the delay.

passage: In her family's house in Tiruvannamalai, Lakshmi had turned the corner table into a study desk: laptop, earphones, and a pile of course certificates. Web design in March. Spreadsheets in May. Python in July. Data analytics in September. Now she was halfway through a cloud course. Her cousin Gargi, home from Chennai for Deepavali, picked up the pile. "Four certificates. How many jobs have you applied for?" Lakshmi kept her eyes on the screen. "After this one. I'm not ready yet." "You said that in March." Lakshmi's jaw tightened. Late that night Gargi found her on the terrace. "What if they all say no?" Lakshmi said at last. "At least with a course, I'm doing something." Gargi sat down beside her. "Then let's get your first no this week, and see that you survive it."

qa.q: What course was Lakshmi halfway through?
qa.a: Lakshmi was halfway through a cloud course.

qa.q: What does Lakshmi's tight jaw suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Lakshmi felt defensive and uneasy, since Gargi had touched the real fear of being rejected.

qa.q: What else could Lakshmi try besides another course?
qa.a: Lakshmi could apply to a handful of entry roles that fit the existing certificates and ask for feedback on any rejections.

qa.q: How might Gargi see Lakshmi's months of courses?
qa.a: Gargi sees them as a way of avoiding applications out of fear, and responds kindly by offering to face the first no together.

grounding: Illustrates a student who keeps adding courses instead of applying, until it emerges that fear of rejection is driving the delay.
